label: Begun populated pasts in every accessible history
definition: PopulatedPastsBegun h Concrete w holds when, in every history v accessible from w, every moment t at which some contingent concrete individual is present has a past with a beginning (BegunAt t: some moment at or before t has no earlier moment). In ordinary language: wherever a contingent thing is present in a possible history, time before it began. Discrete time with a first moment and continuous time with a first moment both satisfy it; an endless discrete past and an open-below continuous past (no first moment) do not. Histories in which no contingent concrete thing is present are unconstrained.
note: Analyst framework definition; attribution deferred. Weak version of founded populated pasts (populatedPastsBegunOfFounded). It denies the begun version of horn H2 of the initial-state view and carries no anti-continuum commitment for time with a first moment. Its cost: in every accessible history it excludes contingent presence in a past with no first moment even when that past is metrically finite, such as a populated standard FLRW Big Bang cosmology, whose time is open below (the initial singularity is not a moment); accepted physical theory treats such models as possible. This is a cost of this necessity claim, not of the possibility premise A3 prime w. Because BegunAt concerns the shared time order, not events, it also excludes empty beginningless time before a first event (creation in an absolute time with no first moment). In a branching order one minimal moment at or below a populated moment suffices, so other branches below it may be beginningless. OPEN.
